account:
Today has been mostly routine mayoral business: a morning grain inspection, lunch at home, an afternoon correspondence session, tea with my neighbour, and a return to the office. I saw seventy-four hay bales at the mill stall. The baker later told me there were eighty loaves for sale at one emerald each; I have not independently checked that bread stock or established daily demand. No council letters were available, and the secretary says no further correspondence or specific bread-access reports have arrived. The town accounts remain an unresolved administrative issue: the records custodian has not been identified, and I have no verified financial figures.

The unusual news is a repeated rumour of a bridge or port change discussed at the bakery. Townspeople named the baker, builder, freight operator and innkeeper as present, but I did not witness that discussion. My neighbour had heard the same rumour without confirmed details. When I asked the baker directly, the baker could not reliably recall a specific proposal or agreement, reported crossing the bridge without trouble this morning, and said the innkeeper knew of no verified obstruction. Thus I do not know that any crossing change actually occurred, nor what such a discussion was intended to accomplish. It might concern transport or market access, but that is only a possibility. The builder or freight operator may have firsthand information.

The baker's concrete concern was matching baking to demand and finding out whether households struggle to afford bread or reach the stall. Neither I nor the secretary has identified specific affected households. I have asked that such reports be brought to the secretary rather than treating rumour as fact.

An eighteen-o'clock great-hall appointment concerns the innkeeper's community hospitality matter. My appointment book says I should attend alone, with no preparation, and that the secretary should remind and escort me. I know no further details of its purpose, and have no evidence connecting it to the crossing rumour. I am now back in the office at seventeen-oh-nine, awaiting business and the evening appointment.
